history.title: A reconstructed history
history.caveat: No source tells this life: every particular of it is ours.
paragraphs: His family is put with Waubansee's band, on the Fox River of the Illinois (about thirty men in May 1812), one of the bands of the Chicago country Governor Edwards described that spring.
He is of the Elk gens (Mis-shă′-wă), and his children are of it after him.
The winter before, he hunted with his family on the Kankakee and traded the skins at Kinzie's for powder, cloth and kettles.
He came in when the bands gathered at Chicago in August, and on the 13th was given cloth and blankets when the goods were handed out.

card_evidence.locator: App. VI, Helm's narrative (1814), Gutenberg #69274 lines 16635-16636
card_evidence.quote: the tribes there assembled to amount of 500 warriors 179 women & children
card_evidence.claim: Helm's count of the gathering at Wells's council.

card_evidence.quote: while in this vicinity they lived in their wigwams near the river, their favorite camping place being at a point on the south bank
card_evidence.claim: Their usual camping place was the State Street creek on the south bank.

card_evidence.quote: beyond which were the groups of Indian wigwams clustered along the creek
card_evidence.claim: The wigwams along the creek, seen from the fort on the last day.

card_evidence.locator: pt. II, ch. II (VI, the right of bestowing names) and ch. VI (the gentes, notes 170 and 172)
card_evidence.quote: These names either proclaimed by their signification the gens to which they belonged, or were known as such by common reputation.
card_evidence.claim: how a reconstructed name is made

card_evidence.quote: In the Fox River ... is another band of Pottawatomies, Chippewas and Ottawas, mixed together
card_evidence.claim: Waubansee's band, the band these cards are put with (reconstructed)

card_evidence.quote: the tribes there assembled to amount of 500 warriors 179 women & children
Their number of warriors was between four and five hundred, mostly of the Potawatamie nation
we were taken back to their encampment near the fort, and distributed among the different tribes
card_evidence.claim: the prisoners brought back to the camp
